title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI Reach ChatGPT's Free Tier
subtitle: OpenAI extended its new conversational interface to Free and Go users on October 8, one day after rolling it out to paid tiers.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT's Chat tab on October 7, 2026, starting with Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. The Free and Go tiers received access on October 8. Paid tiers are backed by GPT-6 Sol; Free and Go are backed by GPT-6 Luna. The change is scoped to the Chat tab — ChatGPT Work and Codex continue to use the models they already shipped with. Enterprise administrators can gate rollout for their own tenants.

Intelligent UI changes what a ChatGPT response can look like. Instead of defaulting to plain text, the model can return graphics, buttons, forms, charts, and small interactive widgets built on request — a recipe with timers inline, road-trip stops on a map, a bill splitter or a savings calculator generated in-conversation. The model picks the format per question and will stay in plain text when that is clearest. Users can also turn down the amount of visual material. OpenAI additionally says GPT-6 begins streaming answers while it is still reasoning, trading some verifiability for perceived speed.

The two-day rollout matters because it closes the capability gap between tiers faster than earlier GPT families did. Historically, OpenAI reserved the newest default model for paid users for weeks or months. Pushing GPT-6 Luna to Free within 24 hours of the paid launch brings the installed base — OpenAI claims 1.2 billion weekly users, a company figure not independently audited — onto roughly current-generation inference almost immediately. That expands who gets to use the Intelligent UI mechanics, and it concentrates even more of day-to-day consumer AI into a single interface.

A takeaway for learners: when a product moves from text-only output to generated UI, the skill of writing a clear prompt matters more, not less. The model now has to choose a format in addition to writing content, and vague prompts will produce busier, less useful screens. Try asking for the format explicitly — 'answer in plain text', 'show a table', 'build a simple calculator' — and watch how the response quality changes. The companies winning in the next year will be the ones whose users learn to drive these new output modes on purpose.
